author: Mynorthwest
title: Curley Challenges Washington State on School Tax Credit as Seattle Teachers Threaten Strike
text:
KIRO host John Curley criticizes Seattle's teachers' union, proposes Federal Scholarship Tax Credit, and discusses the challenges faced by teachers and the district's budget crisis.
KIRO host John Curley has criticized Seattle's teachers' union, suggesting it prioritizes its own power over the well-being of students. Curley's solution to improve education is the Federal Scholarship Tax Credit (FSTC), a $1,700 dollar-for-dollar credit against a taxpayer's federal tax bill that can be directed to any school or tutoring program.
He believes that allowing taxpayers to choose where to direct their tax credits would benefit students and increase parental involvement in education. However, Curley alleges that the teachers' union opposes this idea, fearing that it could lead to a loss of control over education funding. Curley has challenged Washington State Governor Jay Inslee to consider implementing the FSTC before the end of the year.
Meanwhile, Seattle Education Association and Seattle Public Schools are still negotiating a new contract, with 50 bargaining items unresolved. Curley argues that the district's budget crisis is self-inflicted, as it used COVID-19 relief money to fund a labor agreement that it could not sustain, resulting in an $87 million deficit. Curley and KIRO producer Joe Wallace have discussed the challenges faced by teachers, including lack of discipline, increased use of devices in class, and online bullying.
Despite state law making teachers' strikes illegal, Seattle teachers have gone on strike eight times since 1976
